- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or erratic, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check sentiment for bullish reversal — if sentiment drops, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), sentiment may be overly bearish — increase forecast by 5–10% if sentiment recovers or stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price movements by 1–3 periods; adjust forecast to be 1–2% higher than true outcome in early periods if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise — apply smoothing or reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% in high-variance periods.
